Each omino is either a 1×1 square or a horizontal 1×2 domino. Neither can cover cells in two different rows, so the two rows of the 2×10 rectangle are tiled independently.

**Tiling one row.** Let $a_n$ be the number of ways to tile a 1×n strip with squares and horizontal dominoes. Look at the last cell: it is covered either by a square (leaving a 1×(n−1) strip) or by a domino (leaving a 1×(n−2) strip). So

$$a_n = a_{n-1} + a_{n-2},\qquad a_0 = 1,\ a_1 = 1,$$

which gives $a_2 = 2$, $a_3 = 3$, $a_4 = 5$, and so on. These are the Fibonacci numbers, so $a_n = F_{n+1}$. For $n = 10$:

$$a_{10} = F_{11} = 89.$$

**Combining the rows.** Since the rows are independent, the total number of tilings is

$$89 \times 89 = 7921.$$

ANSWER: 7921
